task_message:
Case N09: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 280x280x231 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case N09 is complete. 

**Summary:** I segmented the peripheral nerve sheath tumour in the right thigh — a large, well-defined hyperintense (T2 fat-suppressed) mass arising in the anterior/lateral compartment adjacent to the femur.

**Workflow:**
1. `seg_open` + axial/coronal/sagittal sheets located the mass at roughly axial 100–200, centred on slice ~145.
2. A single positive point on the bright core produced a good first mask (v1, 130 mL).
3. Checked the poles: the ends were thin spurious strands (vessel/fascial fluid), so I applied a morphological opening (r = 3 mm), which trimmed the true extremes and left the mass intact (v2, 127 mL, extent axial 100–201).
4. A positive point at the hazy anterior-inferior periphery caused a large leak back up the bright linear structure; I undid it (−31.5 mL), preferring the tighter contour.
5. Reviewed axial slices 104–195 and sagittal/coronal planes to confirm the outline tracked the lesion edge, then ran `seg_refine` for a small boundary clean-up (v4, 127 mL, 1 component).
6. Final review showed no lesion in any "just-past-the-mask" panel in all three planes; the three automatic candidates were subcutaneous fat/fluid remote from the tumour, so they were rejected.

Final mask: 127.0 mL, single component, saved with medium confidence.
